hero.title: Axonpack ends the guesswork
hero.lead: Answers you and your agent can both read. Every request, error, log and stored value is captured on the device. Your agent can read it from the terminal, and mock or send requests from inside the app.

start.note: The skill reads these docs live, so the agent follows the package's current installation page and checks each step.

agent.title: Reading the running app from the terminal
agent.scene: You ask your coding agent why the profile screen is blank. It reads the code and guesses. Then it asks you to open the app, find the request that failed, and paste the response back into the chat.
agent.answer: With Expo Devtools in the app, the agent can ask the app instead. The devtools command comes with the package and finds the running app through Metro. Its replies are plain text, and you can run the same commands yourself.

steps.text: Lists the apps running on Metro and the device each one is on.
Lists what you can query, such as network, console, storage and crashes, with a row count for each.
Lists the requests that failed in the last 10 minutes. `--where`, `--grep` and `--since` filter any topic.
Prints one row in full. For a request, that is its headers, body and timing.
Answers the app's requests to that URL with a 503 until it reloads. The network topic can also block a URL, or send and replay requests from inside the app. Any method but GET needs `--yes`.

usage.title: The CLI tab
usage.body: It lists what an agent asked or changed, with the reply it got, on the phone and in React Native DevTools. Replies go through your redaction settings, and auth headers and cookies are always masked.
usage.label: The CLI tab, newest first: a DELETE refused for want of --yes, a mocked response, and three queries with how many rows each matched and how long the app took

skills.title: Agent skill
skills.body: One skill covers every package. Your coding agent loads it, and it has the agent read these docs live, so it always matches the latest release. The agent sets the package up in your app with your own package manager and checks each step before the next one.

links.label: Blog post on the devtools command

libraries.title: Packages
libraries.body: Each one is versioned and released on its own. This list is read from npm when the site builds, so everything on it is published.

expo-devtools.scene: A tester says the feed is empty on their phone. On your simulator it loads. There is no cable and no log, and the tester can't tell you which request failed.
expo-devtools.fix: Expo Devtools runs inside the app. The tester taps a button and sees every request with its headers, body and timing, plus the console, crashes, storage and screens. One flag, `enabled`, decides whether any of it runs.

sample.title: app/_layout.tsx

react-native-devtools-tab.scene: You want to know who is signed in while you debug. So you add a `console.log`, reload, read it and delete it. Next week you add it back.
react-native-devtools-tab.fix: React Native DevTools Tab puts a tab of your own beside Console and Sources. The tab is a component that runs in the app, so it reads your real store and its buttons call your real functions. Behind a `__DEV__` guard, a release build carries none of it.

sample.title: devtools.tsx

react-pretty-print.scene: An API answers with a few hundred lines of JSON. On screen it is one `JSON.stringify` inside a `Text`, and you scroll past all of it to find one field.
react-pretty-print.fix: React Pretty Print draws it as a tree that opens and closes, with a preview on every closed node. You pass in your own `View`, `Text` and `Pressable`, so the same component works in React Native and on the web. It has no dependencies and no native module, so it runs in Expo Go.

sample.title: Example.tsx

preview.scene: QA wants to try the login fix from a pull request. The change is only JavaScript, but getting it onto their phone still means a new native build and a wait while it uploads.
preview.fix: Preview publishes one JS bundle per branch to your own S3 bucket. In the app, QA picks the branch from a list, and the app downloads it over the air and restarts into it. Going back to the base build is one tap, and each build lists only the previews made for its native code.

sample.title: Terminal
sample.code:
npx expo install @axonpack/preview expo-file-system
npx preview publish --id task-1-login-fix

in-app-updates.scene: You shipped 2.4.1 with a fix for a crash. A month later the same crash still comes in from people on 2.3.0, who never opened the store to update.
in-app-updates.fix: In-App Updates checks the App Store or Play Store for a newer version and opens an update prompt that already looks right, in light and dark mode. Set a minimum version and anything older has to update. It runs in Expo Go, with no native code to install.

principles.title: Safety and dependencies
principles.body: What the agent tool can reach, and what the packages add to your app. Each point links to the page that explains it.

items.title: Queries are filtered in the app
items.body: The devtools command asks the app over Metro's debugger connection. The app runs the filter and sends back only the rows that match.

items.title: Auth headers and cookies are masked
items.body: The `authorization`, `cookie` and `set-cookie` headers and a page's `document.cookie` always come back as `[redacted]`. Your own redaction settings apply as well.

items.title: Writes to a server need `--yes`
items.body: `send` and `replay` refuse any method but GET without `--yes`. The app checks the flag itself, so a call that skips the command line needs it too.

items.title: Development builds only
items.body: The app answers the command only in a development bundle with the devtools enabled. A release build has nothing it can talk to.

items.title: One native module, loaded optionally
items.body: Expo Devtools has one native module, for the readings JavaScript can't reach. In Expo Go a few of those readings go quiet and the rest of the panel works.

link.label: Expo Go or a development build

items.title: No storage library installed for you
items.body: The Storage tab reads the stores you pass in as adapters, so the package adds no AsyncStorage or MMKV to your app.
